project.title: Wayfire Window Capture
project.summary: A compositor-native Wayfire capture integration that binds each request to an exact window and supplies protocol-managed frames with optional cursor inclusion.

preview.description: An exact toplevel handle resolves to a compositor snapshot and a ready or failed image-copy frame.

blocks.body:
## Make individual windows available to capture clients

Wayfire Window Capture connects the compositor’s window model to the ext image-capture protocols. A client obtains a foreign-toplevel handle, creates a capture source for that window, and requests frames through the image-copy protocol.

I developed the integration to support uses such as live taskbar previews and window-specific screen sharing. The active implementation is now built inside Wayfire Desktop. The original standalone package remains an archived source reference, and its milestones are retained below.

## Use compositor identity to choose the window

The capture manager resolves the handle’s attached view pointer against the compositor’s live views. A valid mapped view with an output becomes the source. Missing or unavailable views produce an inert source instead of selecting another window with a similar name.

That distinction matters when several windows share an application ID and title: display metadata can describe them, while the handle selects the exact view that supplies the pixels.

## Keep the frame contract explicit

The maintained implementation snapshots the view when a frame is requested and updates size constraints when its dimensions change. It currently advertises ARGB8888 and XRGB8888 shared-memory formats; DMA-BUF constraints are withheld until they can be derived from the actual backing buffer.

Cursor inclusion is checked per frame and rendered into a separate snapshot when requested. Unmapped views, missing buffers, and copy failures follow the protocol’s failure path, giving clients a definite outcome.

## Carry reliability work into compositor maintenance

Earlier milestones established distinct capture identities, explicit format negotiation, optional cursors, and recovery during output stalls and monitor changes. Moving the plugin in-tree brought it alongside the Wayfire and wlroots versions whose lifetime and rendering APIs it uses.

The current source owns the capture-source manager and releases snapshot buffers when the final session stops. The project’s history records how those boundaries evolved, including mechanisms specific to the former standalone implementation.
